Counsel for Respondent :- Anuj Pratap Singh,C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for quashing of the notification dated 23.11.1989 under Section 4 read with Section 17(4) and notification dated 27.11.1990 under Section 6 read with Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') in respect of the land of the petitioners bearing plot Nos. 1/2, 2, 3, 4 Ka, 4 Kha, 5, 8, 11, 14, 16, 19/2, 19/3, 19/4, 28/1, 28/2, 29,
30/1, 31, 32, 36, 39, 40, 43, 48, 53, 56, 62, 72/2, 73, 102 Ka, 110, 177 Ka, 115, 122, 124, 125, 133, 138,
142, 143, 144, 145, 146, 147, 148, 150, 151, 161, 164, 167, 168, 170, 171, 200, 381/9, 381/11 situated at Village Behata, Tehsil and Pargana Hathras, District Aligarh.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that invocation of the urgency provisions under the Act and dispensation of the inquiry under Section 5-A was wholly illegal as the acquisition was for planned industrial development and it has already been held by the Supreme Court in the case of Radhy Shyam (Dead) Through LRS and others Vs. State of U.P. and others: (2011) 5 SCC 553 that urgency clause could not be invoked for such purpose.

entities.text: Radhy Shyam (Dead) Through LRS and others Vs. State of U.P. and others: (2011) 5 SCC 553
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Sri Pankaj Rai, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no.2, submits that the acquisition proceedings were completed long back.
Possession was taken on 24.06.1992 and award was declared on 25.05.1993.
The petitioners cannot challenge the acquisition proceedings after three decades.
The petition is liable to be dismissed on ground of delay and laches.
4. We find considerable force in the submission of learned counsel for respondent no.2.
It is not disputed rather admitted to the petitioners that award was declared on 25.05.1993.
Learned counsel for the petitioners admits, during course of oral submissions, that the petitioners had also received compensation.

5. In such view of the matter, we are of the considered opinion that the writ petition is highly belated and, at this distance in time, we decline to examine the issue regarding wrongful invocation of urgency provisions.

Order Date :- 10.5.2024 AKShukla/-
(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
